acceptanceCriteria.statement: The target pose is SOLVED from the panel's own measured shape and the camera's own optics, never typed. Given a panel's metrics and a fill fraction f, the pose function returns a distance d = (height/2) / tan(f × fov/2), so the panel subtends exactly f of the vertical field of view. Feeding it a panel of a different size or aspect must move the distance proportionally, and feeding it a different FOV must too — a function that returns the same number for a 0.240 m panel and a 0.450 m panel has a constant hidden in it. This is Max's flexibility constraint stated at the smallest scale where it can be proved. It is a PURE function with no three.js import, because the maths must be provable without a browser and the same maths must be what the game runs.

verifyVia.input: Call the pose solver headless with the two panel sizes that have actually shipped on this project (0.450 × 0.300 m, 3:2 and 0.240 × 0.200 m, 6:5), at the game's 70° FOV, across fill fractions.
verifyVia.observable: Each returned distance re-projects to the requested fill fraction within 1e-6. The two panel sizes return DIFFERENT distances in the ratio of their heights. Changing the FOV alone changes the distance. No literal distance, centre, normal or corner id appears anywhere in the module.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Rigging a panel for motion does not move it. Every node in cockpit.glb is a flat root with world-baked vertices and no transform, so wrapping a screen in a pivot group at its measured centre and reparenting the mesh must leave the panel's world position bit-unchanged — rest pose is identity by construction, not by a remembered constant. Measured the only way that proves it: re-run measureQuad on the rigged mesh's world vertices and compare against the pre-rig measurement. This is what makes 're-fit the screens and nothing needs re-typing' true rather than aspirational.

verifyVia.input: Measure each Screen_* quad, rig it (pivot group + reparent, glass AND its ScreenBody_* housing), then measure again through the same measureQuad path — and separately, rig a panel, zoom it, dismiss it, and measure a third time.
verifyVia.observable: width, height, aspect, centre and normal are identical before and after rigging, and identical again after a full zoom-and-dismiss round trip. The pivot group's transform is identity at rest.

verification.evidence: Verified at 7203c49. The rig composes to identity because the pivot sits at the measured centre with the mesh at local -centre, so "rest" is the identity transform rather than a number anyone wrote down.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The pointer adapter delivers _handleClick, which is the single gap that blocks 'interact with the full menu' — PanelPointer.js forwarded only _handleMouseDown/Move/Up, and _handleClick is the sole route to the level tabs, the SYSTEM sub-views, the autopilot toggle and the BURN/WARP commit. The click fires AFTER the release (preserving the existing load-bearing ordering, which exists because _place throws on a zero-sized buffer and must never take the drag hostage) but with the panel pixel already placed, because _handleClick reads _dragStartX/_dragStartY. ⚠ AMENDED 2026-07-29 DURING BUILD: the drag rejection is NOT the adapter's. NavComputer already owns it — it compares against _dragStartX/Y and bails past 25 px² — and a browser fires click after mouseup regardless and lets that check decide, so forwarding unconditionally is the faithful port. A second threshold in the adapter would give one rule two homes to drift between, and the drift would surface as clicks that work at the centre of a pan and not at its edges. What the adapter owns is whether the gesture belongs to this panel at all: press AND release both on the glass. The 25 px² rule itself is exercised against the real class under AC-ZOOMED-IS-OPERABLE.

verifyVia.input: Against a NavComputer-shaped stub, headless, at two unlike buffer sizes: press+release on the glass; press then a release that misses; a release with no preceding press; a press whose drag already slid off and spent its release; a release whose buffer has collapsed to zero; and a target with no _handleClick at all.
verifyVia.observable: One click for the first, ordered strictly after _handleMouseUp and with the position already equal to uv x buffer size. Zero clicks for every other case. The collapsed buffer still throws AND still released the drag. The click-less target does not throw. Zero getBoundingClientRect calls throughout — the stub's throws, so the DOM path cannot have run.

verification.evidence: Verified at 1a9628d. Re-confirmed LIVE at this sha: drillToPopulatedSystem drove a real clickGlass press at buffer px [299.61, 257.83], uvError [-1.7e-16, 2.2e-16], routed to the nav adapter, and the nav computer fell into SYSTEM.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The travel is cubic-out and it LANDS — at t=1 the pose equals the target exactly, with no overshoot and no residual offset that leaves the panel a millimetre off where it was solved to be. Cubic-out rather than smoothstep is the house taste datum, recorded when Max evaluated curves for AutopilotMotion and chose it for its firmer terminal landing; smoothstep's asymptotic tail read as mushy. Duration, fill fraction and the park-vs-head-lock choice are all knobs, not constants, because they are judge-by-eye questions and the lab is where Max answers those.

verifyVia.input: Step the mover headless from rest to zoomed across the full duration at fixed dt, then past the end; then step it back.
verifyVia.observable: Position and orientation at t=1 equal the solved target to floating-point tolerance; no sample overshoots past the target; stepping beyond the duration changes nothing further. The reverse trip lands on the measured rest pose, not on a cached copy of it. The easing samples match a cubic-out curve, not smoothstep.

designDecisions: WHOLE MONITOR TRAVELS, ARM STAYS. Max chose this on 2026-07-29 from three mock-ups, over glass-only (which leaves a dark empty socket) and over a non-moving expanded copy (which contradicts his standing ruling that the SCREEN travels to the eye, and would pay for the nav render twice). The preview he selected showed the arm left behind as a stub, so that is accepted rather than open.

PIVOT GROUPS, NOT GEOMETRY EDITS. Every GLB node is a flat root with world-baked vertices, so a pivot group at metrics.centre with the mesh at local −centre reproduces the rest pose exactly and makes identity the resting transform. This is why 're-fit the screens and nothing needs re-typing' is structural rather than a discipline anyone has to remember.

HEIGHT BINDS, NOT WIDTH. Panel aspect 1.200 against a 16:9 view: a 6:5 panel physically cannot fill the view edge-to-edge without stretching its content. It fills top-to-bottom with side margins. Worth stating in the contract so 'it doesn't fill the whole screen' is not later filed as a bug.

CUBIC-OUT, ~400 ms. Cubic-out is the recorded house taste datum — Max evaluated curves for AutopilotMotion and chose it over smoothstep for the firmer terminal landing. ~400 ms matches NavComputer's own drill animations (350/400/500 ms), so the panel's travel and the map's drills feel like one machine. Both are knobs.

PARKED, NOT HEAD-LOCKED — with a toggle. The target pose is solved from the camera at the instant of zoom and then held in cockpit space, so increment 4's head-sway gives the panel parallax instead of welding a screen to the pilot's face. Exposed as a lab toggle because it is a judge-by-eye question and Max is the judge.

activate() IS NOT CALLED. It would buy keyboard navigation and the search box, but _ensureSearchDom returns early on a canvas with no parentElement so search cannot work on glass anyway, and activate() registers capture-phase handlers that swallow the pilot's own W/A/S/D/R/F. Mouse alone reaches the entire menu. Recorded as a non-goal, not an oversight.

GENERIC MECHANISM, NAV-ONLY WIRING. Max's 'only necessary for the upper-left' and his 'make the system flexible' pull in opposite directions if both are read as scope. They are not the same requirement: 'flexible' is about screen POSITIONS moving, which the metrics-derived design answers by construction; 'only the upper-left' is about which panel the player can zoom, which is wiring. Building the mechanism for four costs nothing over building it for one.

THE ESC CHANGE SUPERSEDES AC-NAV-OVERLAY-UNCHANGED, FOR THE ESCAPE PATH ONLY. That AC is green in cockpit-screen-content-2026-07-28 and this workstream deliberately breaks part of it, on Max's explicit 2026-07-29 ruling that ESC should mean dismiss everywhere. A requirement Max changed is not a regression — but it is recorded here rather than left for someone to discover as a contradiction between two contracts.

NavPanel.test.js's SOURCE PIN MUST BE AMENDED, NOT LOOSENED. It pins the literal line `if (nav) nav.chromeless = true;` and gutting that line is how it proves it bites. The conditional write requires updating the pin, which is indistinguishable in a diff from quietly weakening it — so AC-BASELINE-GREEN requires the amended pin to still turn red when the write is removed.

AMENDED DURING BUILD — THE HEADLESS HARNESS. NavSource.js's header asserts that a real NavComputer cannot be constructed in a test 'at any depth, by any arrangement'. That is false: a stub canvas, a Proxy 2D context and a document shim are enough. The escape ACs were scoped expecting source scans and are verified against the real class instead. This is NOT the full render-based regression suite on the debt list — the context draws nothing, so it answers what the class DID, never what it looked like.

AMENDED DURING BUILD — handleEscape() SURVIVES, with one caller. Unwiring ESC is a single line in main.js. The method stays because NavComputer._handleClick routes `e.button === 2` through it, and right-click-to-go-back is a separate shipped affordance Max did not ask to change. A method named handleEscape that Escape no longer calls is a trap, so the binding is asserted in the test file rather than left to be discovered.

PARKED vs HEAD-LOCKED. Built parked, exposed as a toggle. If free-look while zoomed turns out to matter, this is the knob that answers it.
